summary: agent_runs.created_at is IMMUTABLE after insert (cinatra#2911) — the operator-upgrade twin of the fresh-install bootstrap leaf agentRunCreatedAtSchemaQueries in src/lib/agent-run-created-at-schema.ts, spread into buildCreateStoreSchemaQueries in the SAME PR. THE DEFECT: the bootstrap DDL carried, with no WHERE clause, UPDATE agent_runs SET created_at = COALESCE(started_at, completed_at, created_at) immediately after the idempotent ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS created_at. The surrounding DDL is idempotent; that UPDATE was idempotent only against FIXED inputs, and started_at / completed_at are populated LATER in a run's life. ensurePostgresSchema replays the WHOLE list once per fresh server process (the globalThis flag and the pid-keyed done-marker skip it only within one process), so every restart recomputed created_at from data that did not exist when the row was inserted: a run that had reached running reported started_at as its creation time, and a run that FAILED before it started reported completed_at — its own end time — while the child rows it owns appeared to predate it. created_at is the only record of when a run was REQUESTED and the run listings order by it, so the loss was silent and irreversible. WHY THIS MIGRATION EXISTS: the versioned chain carried NOTHING for this column — an operator database only ever received created_at from the bootstrap DDL, which runs AHEAD of the chain — so the chain and the fresh-install path disagreed about who owns the column. This module ships the SAME three idempotent statements the leaf now emits, so both paths land on one shape and the immutable form is recorded in versioned history rather than only in bootstrap text. SHAPE: the column is added NULLABLE and WITHOUT a default, which is what makes 'never had a creation timestamp' distinguishable from 'already carries one' — a row that predates the column lands on NULL, a row that already has a value keeps it because the backfill narrows on created_at IS NULL; the default and the NOT NULL are applied AFTERWARDS so the final shape is exactly what it was (timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()) and the insert path keeps relying on the database default. Adding the column WITH a default would defeat the guard: PostgreSQL fills every existing row with it, so nothing would be NULL. ON AN ALREADY-BOOTSTRAPPED DATABASE — every deployed instance, since the column has existed since the agent_runs consolidation — all three statements are no-ops: the column exists, no row is NULL, the default and the constraint are in place (SET NOT NULL skips its validation scan when attnotnull is already set). Nothing is rewritten; after this migration NO path recomputes a present created_at from another column. DESTRUCTIVE by the convention's enumeration (a data rewrite plus a SET NOT NULL on an existing table), though both are strictly NARROWER than what shipped before: the backfill it replaces had no predicate at all, and the NOT NULL restores a constraint the column already carries on every deployed instance. NO BACKFILL OF ALREADY-CORRUPTED VALUES, deliberately: a created_at collapsed onto started_at or completed_at is indistinguishable from one that was always that value and the pre-replay value is stored nowhere — this change stops further loss, it cannot reconstruct what earlier replays destroyed. Unqualified names ride the runner's search_path (the app schema). down() is intentionally a no-op: the forward shape IS the deployed shape, and dropping the column would destroy every run's creation time while re-widening it or re-installing the unguarded rewrite would reinstate the defect. SEQ 0096 — strictly greater than the max shipped seq on origin/main (core__0095 run-recommendation-skip-record). migrations/** is HIGH-RISK: owner approval required; the lane never merges.
